newsitem.title: INDIA: Bank of India's 6.75 bln rupee IPO opens on Feb 21.
newsitem.headline: Bank of India's 6.75 bln rupee IPO opens on Feb 21.

text.p: A 6.75 billion rupees maiden public equity issue by the Bank of India, one of the country's leading state-run banks, will open for subscription on February 21, the bank said on Tuesday.
The price for the initial public offer (IPO) is 45 rupees per share of 10 rupees face value.

Government holding in the wholly state-owned bank would fall to 76.52 percent after the IPO, bank chief G. Kathuria told a press conference, adding it is authorised to reduce the state's stake to 49 percent.

After reserving for preferential allotments to Indian financial institutions, banks, expatriate Indians, mutual funds and employees, the net offer to Indian public is 3.15 billion rupees, the bank said.
There is no reservation for foreign financial institutions in the proposed issue, but the bank intends to make a global depositary receipts issue in a year's time, Kathuria said.
The bank topped state-run banks last year, with a net profit of 2.76 billion rupees in 1995/96 (April-March) -- a big turnaround after making huge losses in 1992/93 and 1993/94.

Kathuria told reporters that non-performing assets as a ratio to total credit will be brought down to 5.0 percent in the year to March 31, 1997 from 7.0 percent a year ago and compared to 32 percent a few years earlier.
"Profitability is the basic focus," he said. "We have undertaken a total restructuring with this objective in mind."
The bank recorded a net profit of 2.11 billion rupees in the six months to September 30, 1996.
"It's during the second half that profits are much higher," said B.V. Goud, chief general manager at Industrial Development Bank of India, a lead manager to the issue.
The bank has 2,437 branches with 19 overseas branches in four continents and employees 56,000 people. Total global deposits was 275.23 billion at end March 1996, the bank said.
